searchText: Is there a place I can see the latest, up-to-date bellatrix consensus specs? The `specs` folder of the `ethereum/consensus-specs` repo only seems to show the changes of the individual changes but not the current state of the spec as a whole? you'll need to backfill with "unchanged" stuff you could also run this: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/Makefile#L99 and it will write the "compiled" specs to your local machine These are normally released here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases The fixtures.tar.gz file contains the generated json tests Thanks. I can see you are putting some interesting values to storage. Have you considered logs? For logs we only have non-standard "logs hash", right? Thanks thx This is the current flow of the interactions between spec tests filler and the t8n/b11r, we are basically forwarding the rlp we get from the t8n tool, but we can simply pass again the same json we originally sent to the t8n It would be great to make it possible ok I will make this change today, I'd like to know a bit more about your setup, are you currently modifying the exec-spec-tests code to call a different b11r binary ? No, I implemented RLP decoding in evmone but after team suggestion I just decided to ask if it's possible to do it with json only. I haven't started using exec-spec-tests with evmone yet. We have t8n implemented and tested with ethereum/tests ok great, I think we can make the evm implementation selectable for exec-spec-tests when the user wants to fill the tests, so it should be very easy to swap between geth's evm, evmone or any other implementation ~~How do you best use input/output arguments for both `t8n` using `evmone`? In geth `evm t8n` for example we use --input.txs (json) and --output.txs (rlp) directly within exec-spec-tests.?~~ Found the cli args in `t8n.cpp`

excerpts.author: philogy
excerpts.content: Is there a place I can see the latest, up-to-date bellatrix consensus specs? The `specs` folder of the `ethereum/consensus-specs` repo only seems to show the changes of the individual changes but not the current state of the spec as a whole?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: you'll need to backfill with "unchanged" stuff

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
you  could also run this: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/Makefile#L99

and it will write the "compiled" specs to your local machine

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
These are normally released here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases
The fixtures.tar.gz file contains the generated json tests

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content:
Thanks.

I can see you are putting some interesting values to storage. Have you considered logs? For logs we only have non-standard "logs hash", right?

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: This is the current flow of the interactions between spec tests filler and the t8n/b11r, we are basically forwarding the rlp we get from the t8n tool, but we can simply pass again the same json we originally sent to the t8n

excerpts.author: rodiazet
excerpts.content: It would be great to make it possible

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: ok I will make this change today, I'd like to know a bit more about your setup, are you currently modifying the exec-spec-tests code to call a different b11r binary ?

excerpts.author: rodiazet
excerpts.content: No, I implemented RLP decoding in evmone but after team suggestion I just decided to ask if it's possible to do it with json only.

excerpts.author: rodiazet
excerpts.content: I haven't started using exec-spec-tests with evmone yet. We have t8n implemented and tested with ethereum/tests

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: ok great, I think we can make the evm implementation selectable for exec-spec-tests when the user wants to fill the tests, so it should be very easy to swap between geth's evm, evmone or any other implementation

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content:
~~How do you best use input/output arguments for both `t8n`  using `evmone`?  In geth `evm t8n`  for example we use --input.txs (json) and --output.txs (rlp) directly within exec-spec-tests.?~~
Found the cli args in `t8n.cpp`
